title: Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a convergent subsequence
statement: Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence of real numbers that is bounded: there is $M$ with $|a_n| \le M$ for every $n$. Then $(a_n)$ has a convergent subsequence: there are a strictly increasing $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $L \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a_{\varphi(n)} \to L$.
binders: (a : ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ n, |a n| ≤ M)
claim: ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∃ L : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto (a ∘ φ) Filter.atTop (nhds L)

steps.text: Since $(a_n)$ is bounded, there is $M$ with $|a_n| \le M$ for every $n$, so every term lies in the closed interval $[-M, M]$, a bounded set.
fragment: have hbd : Bornology.IsBounded (Set.range a) := (Metric.isBounded_Icc (-M) M).subset (by rintro _ ⟨n, rfl⟩; exact abs_le.mp (hM n))

steps.text: The interval $[-M, M]$ is compact, so a sequence in it has a convergent subsequence: there are a strictly increasing $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $L \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a_{\varphi(n)} \to L$.
fragment: obtain ⟨L, -, φ, hφ, hL⟩ := tendsto_subseq_of_bounded hbd (fun n => Set.mem_range_self n)

steps.text: Hence $(a_{\varphi(n)})$ is a convergent subsequence of $(a_n)$, as claimed.
